reputation.summary: The ubiquitous cheap BiFET, which TI calls 'ideally suited for high-fidelity and audio preamplifier applications'. Enthusiasts treat it as the stock part that upgrades (OPA2134, NE5532) are judged against. JFET input and low distortion suit filters, tone controls and crossovers, not low-impedance high-gain stages. Douglas Self, NwAvGuy and Cycfi compare it; synth forums discuss TI's doubled noise spec.
typical_uses: DAC low-pass filters and output stages
sound cards, USB interfaces, active speakers, headphone amps
active crossovers, EQ and tone controls in mixers
caveats: Legacy die reverses phase near V−; needs 10 V minimum supply, so unusable at 5 V.
Only ±10 V min into 2 kΩ: weak for 600 Ω or headphone loads.
Since PCN 20221219006.1 the same part number may be the new die: ~6 dB noisier, lower THD+N.
TL074CDR date codes 2436/2443/2522 failed a customer test: output swung to −13 V, not −11.5 V.
TL071 D/P lost offset-null pins (Rev W); new-die inputs are diode-clamped (VS+0.2 V, 10 mA).

counterfeit_notes: TL072 itself is too cheap to fake but reportedly hides inside remarked OPA2604, OPA2134 and OPA1612 (TL082). Check for solvent-removable marks, resurfaced tops, ~1.4 mA/ch, ~3 MHz. Genuine post-2023 TI parts may be the new die (37 nV/√Hz, ~0.94 mA/ch).

silicon_changes.identification: H in the orderable (TL072HIDR, TL074HIDR, TL071HIDBVR…), I-grade only. Top mark 'TL072D' may be an H die. Rev W: H = latest flow (CSO: RFB).
silicon_changes.summary: TI's next-generation TL07x: a new die on a 'modern process' inside SLOS080. Rail-inclusive (V+) input, clamped inputs, lower Iq, higher GBW and slew, far lower Vos and Ib, about twice the noise. TL072H production Jun 2021 (Rev R), TL071H Jul 2021 (Rev S). Now called 'FET-input'.

spec_deltas.before: +/-5 to +/-15 V rec., 36 V abs max (30 V part-page headline)
V- +4 V to V+ (rec.), phase reversal near V-
spec_deltas.after: V- +1.5 V to V+, no phase reversal; inputs clamped (diff <= VS+0.2 V, 10 mA)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: About 6 dB more noise at 1 kHz hurts low-impedance high-gain stages; distortion, slew, headroom and supply current improve.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: same pinout, but noise doubles, TL071H SOIC lacks offset null, input clamps differ.
silicon_changes.verification: Based on SLOS080 Revs O–W and the TL072HIDR part page; TI datasheet listing confirms H parts.

silicon_changes.identification: Same part number and marking. Legacy die likely before date codes ~2238 (PCN 20220615003.1 parts) or ~2312. New die: ~0.94 mA/ch, 37 nV/√Hz, swings to negative rail.
silicon_changes.summary: PCNs 20220615003.1 (Jun 2022; TL071CDR, TL072CDRG4) and 20221219006.1 (Dec 2022; TL072/TL074 list) moved plain C/AC/BC/I grades from Sherman to RFAB with die rev C→A and MLA assembly. Same die as TL07xH, with new ESD and clamp diodes to VCC+. Rev U specs new-die values; Rev W says either flow ships.

spec_deltas.parameter: Negative output saturation (E2E TL074CDR report, VCC- = -13 V)

spec_deltas.after: updated ESD structures and protection scheme; clamp diodes to VCC+ (TI E2E replies)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Re-populated boards may gain ~6 dB hiss but lower distortion; clipping differs; units vary; TL071 trim lost.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pin-compatible but noisier, different clipping; high for TL071 sockets using a pins 1/5 trimmer.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN summaries list TL071CDR and TL072CDRG4; E2E threads 1453480 and 1428797 confirm failures and clamp diodes.

silicon_changes.summary: ST's second-source die has its own specs: lower noise and higher bandwidth than TI's legacy die. A different vendor's die under the same generic number; no ST PCN found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: On paper ST is now the lowest-noise TL072, since TI's plain TL072 specs 37 nV/√Hz.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same pinout and supply class.
silicon_changes.verification: ST tl074.pdf (Nov 2013) seen in search results, matching the cited revision.
